newsitem.title: USA: Motorola, Daewoo Telecom consortium gets contract.
newsitem.headline: Motorola, Daewoo Telecom consortium gets contract.

text.p: Motorola Inc's Asia Pacific Cellular Infrastructure Group said its consortium with Daewoo Telecom was awarded a $180 million network contract in Seoul, South Korea.
Under the contract with Korea Telecom Freetel (KTF), the consortium will deploy a code division multiple access (CDMA) digital wireless phone network in Seoul, Motorola said.
KTF will use Motorola's SC 4820 base station equipment and Centralized Base Site Controller equipment and Daewoo PCX switches for its new Personal Communications Service network.
Product shipment will begin in the second quarter of 1997, with the first phase of commercial deployment scheduled for early 1998, Motorola said.
The CDMA network will serve subscribers from western Seoul to Inchon. The system provided by Daewoo and Motorola will have the capacity to serve up to 300,000 subscribers.
Daewoo Telecom provides telecommunications equipment and invests in telecommunications service providers.
Motorola provides wireless communications, semiconductors, and advanced electronic systems, components and services.
